title: Backfill + Gating for Trusted Prompt Bundles (golden datasets) and Eval Regression Alerts
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: We lack an operational workflow that ensures changes to model configs, runtime flags, or deployed model variants are automatically checked against curated 'trusted' prompt bundles (golden datasets). This leads to silent regressions and manual, ad-hoc verification.

Goal: Implement a backfill and gating pipeline that ties prompt-set versioning + RBAC-managed golden datasets to our eval pipelines so that: (1) every model/config change triggers deterministic evals on the latest trusted prompt bundles, (2) historical releases can be backfilled and re-scored, (3) CI can gate merges when regressions exceed thresholds, and (4) we surface actionable alerts and audit logs for operators and PMs.

Scope:
- Prompt set metadata: enforce required fields (curator, intent tags, trust-level, locked flag, canonical-version).
- RBAC: UI and API surfaces to lock/unlock golden bundles and restrict who can create new canonical versions.
- Versioning: implement immutable snapshot IDs for golden bundles and support references in eval jobs and deployment manifests.
- Backfill: a scalable backfill job runner to re-run evals across historical model variants and config snapshots.
- Gating: CI integration + GitHub check that runs a subset of golden evals on PRs that touch runtime or model mapping code; fail PRs on P0 regressions.
- Alerts: threshold-based regression alerts with suggested rollbacks and links to failing prompt examples.
- Auditability: persist who approved canonical versions and when; link to related PRs and console rollout IDs.

Out-of-scope for initial iteration: advanced UI workflows for collaborative curation (will follow in a separate design ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Golden bundle metadata schema enforced in API; attempt to create without required fields returns 400 and validation errors.
2) RBAC rules applied: only users in 'prompt-curators' group or admins can mark a bundle as canonical/locked; API and Console respect this.
3) Snapshot IDs produced for canonical bundles and immutable once created; eval jobs accept snapshot ID reference and use exact prompt set.
4) Backfill runner documented and able to re-run evals for at least 50 historical model/config snapshots in <= 6 hours for our current test corpus size; produces per-prompt diffs.
5) CI gating: a lightweight eval job runs on PRs touching runtime or model-mapping code; PR check fails when a regression exceeds the configured severity threshold (configurable per repo).

6) Alerting: regression alerts sent to #eval-regressions Slack channel and create an incident ticket when high-impact regressions detected; alert includes top 10 failing prompts and links to the failing model/config.
7) Audit log entries created for operations that change canonical bundle state and for CI gating failures; entries include user, timestamp, and related PR/rollout IDs.
